subject: bolas spider
title: This Spider Spins No Web. It Fakes Perfume and Swings a Glue Ball

scenes.text: This spider catches moths without a web. It lies to them.
By day it sits on a leaf disguised as a bird dropping. By night it hangs from a thread holding one sticky ball.
Then it releases a scent: a copy of the perfume a female moth uses to call a mate. Male moths fly straight in.
The spider feels the wingbeats, swings the ball and lassoes the moth out of the air.
Its two favourite moths fly at different hours, so the spider changes its fake perfume as the night goes on.
Catch nothing? It eats the ball and tries again tomorrow. No web, no chase. Just a lie and one swing.

description:
The bolas spider never builds a web. It hangs from a thread with a single sticky droplet and releases chemicals that copy the sex pheromone of female moths, so male moths fly to it; it then swings the ball and snags them in mid-air.
University of Kentucky entomologists found that two moth species make up more than 90 percent of its catch, and that the spider adjusts its chemical blend through the night to match whichever moth is flying. By day it looks like a bird dropping; if it catches nothing, it eats the ball and recycles the silk.
Is this the sneakiest hunter in nature? Comment below.
thumbnail_text: NO WEB. ONE LIE. ONE SWING.
first_comment: The sticky ball is only about 2.5 millimetres across, and its glue is built in two layers: a thin fluid that seeps under the moth's scales and a thick one that holds the thread. What other animal that lies to its prey should we cover?
